name: Crawler Crane
instructions: omr/instructions/9391-1-1.pdf (the crawler crane); omr/instructions/9391-1-2.pdf builds the alternate bulldozer

functions.does: The black gear at the back end of the undercarriage slews the crane: its long axle runs under the turntable, where a bevel gear drives the turntable's teeth, turning the whole upper works with the boom.
functions.source: book: steps 2-7 (turntable, the long axle with its bevel gear under it and the knob on the end); how it's worked inferred, as the book draws no arrow for it

functions.does: The black gear at the top back of the upper works raises and lowers the boom: it turns a worm, which turns a small gear on a cross axle, whose cranks push the boom up on two links.
functions.source: book: sub-steps 1-10 on pages 12-16 (the worm, gear, cranks and links), step 25 (the arrows show the knob turning and the boom swinging)

functions.does: The black gear on the left side at the back of the upper works winds the winch, raising or lowering the hook on its string over the boom tip.
functions.source: book: sub-steps 1-4 on pages 26-27 and step 20 (the winch axle and string), steps 29-31 (the string over the boom tip; arrows show the knob turning and the string running)

functions.does: A small gear on a friction axle pin meshes with the gear on the winch axle, so the winch turns stiffly and holds the hook where it's left.
functions.source: inferred: the second small gear beside the winch, on a blue axle pin, has no other use

functions.does: The two tracks run round their sprockets and idlers, so the crane rolls along; nothing drives them.
